name: CA-17
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans 21 points Democratic, giving Khanna a large structural edge
Khanna holds a massive financial advantage: $16.6 million on hand versus about $5,000 for Tandon
Prediction markets price Khanna near 97 percent to win
No public general-election polling exists, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 21-point Democratic lean, Khanna's incumbency, and a roughly 270-to-1 cash advantage make an upset implausible, and markets agree at 97 percent. The 2022 environment trims a few points off the fundamentals but nowhere near enough to threaten the outcome.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a far closer race, or a major late development involving Khanna, would be the main signal that this is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ro Khanna, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a Silicon Valley district that leans 21 points Democratic. He has raised more than $15 million and holds over $16 million in cash, while Republican Ritesh Tandon has raised about $57,000 with roughly $5,000 available. Prediction markets price Khanna's chances near 97 percent.

No public general-election polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the enormous spending gap. The 2022 national environment favors Republicans by a few points, but that is far from enough to overcome the district's fundamentals. Tandon would need an extraordinary shift to make this competitive; the realistic question is the size of Khanna's winning margin rather than the outcome.
